as_of.score_formula: 100 * sum(w_i * d_i for observed i) / sum(w_i for observed i) / 2, with d_i in {-2,-1,+1,+2}
as_of.current_stance_formula: decay-weighted average of agreed event scores in the 90-day window; weight = 0.5 ** (days / 30)
as_of.structural_lean_formula: equal-weighted average of agreed event scores in 2025-05-20..as-of; published only if at least 4 agreed events and at least 365 days between first and last
as_of.disagreement_rule: Pass A and Pass B must match on the sign of the event score and on every observed dimension, and coverage must differ by less than 20 percentage points. Otherwise do not average. A reasoned third pass may resolve a disagreement if 2 of 3 readings agree; if it stays close, mark unresolved and exclude.

vorbehalte: Weights (40/20/20/10/10), camp thresholds (±20), alert thresholds (15 / 25 points) and the 30-day half-life are proposed model parameters and are not validated (nicht validiert / not validated).

Structural lean is the equal-weighted average of agreed event scores in the 12–18 month window 20 May 2025 to 20 November 2026. It is published only when there are at least 4 agreed scored policy events and at least 365 days between the first and last of those events. Shorter official tenure (Warsh as Chair from 22 May 2026; Venable as Interim Atlanta President, first official message 12 May 2026) is labelled insufficient evidence even if a current stance can be computed.

Current stance is the 90-day decay-weighted average of agreed event scores (half-life 30 days). A current-stance camp is printed only when a published stance exists and at least one agreed event in that 90-day window has an observed preferred-rate-path dimension (same rule as Phase 2). That camp is not a structural classification.
The public camp field is the structural classification (Hawk / Centrist / Dove / insufficient evidence). Current stance and its camp are shown alongside it.

Phase-2 events keep their original independent Pass A and Pass B. A reasoned third pass was run on the seven Phase-2 disagreements. Five were resolved by 2-of-3 agreement and are included with recomputed scores. Two (Schmid 15.11.2026 and Barkin 9.11.2026) remain nicht aufgelöst / unresolved and are excluded from calculations.

Phase 3.1 is a delta rerun that two-pass scored remaining policy-relevant official texts already stored under phase3/raw/ for 20 May 2025–20 November 2026. No new crawl was run. Two FOMC statements (17 June and 16 September 2026) were re-fetched with curl only to confirm the official 12-0 votes; no missed dissents were found. Pass A and Pass B were coded from the same official verbatim quotes with a conservative rubric (conditional scenarios are not a baseline path; missing dimensions stay not_observed, never 0). They agree where that official language is explicit. Identical or near-verbatim repeat speeches and official dissent explainers already scored in v3 were treated as syndication and excluded from the calculations. Official texts with no observed dimension, and non-policy official texts, are listed internally and are not in the public events table.

Every scored quote used in site_data_v3_1 is verbatim from an official Board or Reserve Bank page, official PDF, or FOMC statement stored in this package. Licensed-press wording is not in site_data_v3_1. Interviews without an official transcript remain unconfirmed and are not scored. A primary-source date correction was applied to one Kansas City speech: the stored filename used 12 November 2026, but the official datePublished is 18 September 2026.

Speeches without monetary-policy path or stance content stay out of the public events table. Missing dimensions are coded 'not observed', never 0. Allowed dimension codes are {-2,-1,+1,+2} or not_observed.

Event scores use observed dimensions only, with weights renormalised and then scaled by 1/2 to the -100..+100 range. A single observed dimension therefore renormalises to ±50 or ±100. Coverage and confidence are published with the score.

2026 voter status is taken from the official FOMC membership page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm, last update 18 November 2026). The seven Board seats are filled (no vacancy). Cheryl Venable is Interim President of the Atlanta Fed. Sushmita Shukla is listed as a 2026 alternate (New York First Vice President) but is not a president and is not scored. Primary-source dates are used throughout.
Relative shift is a diagnostic (own latest-vs-baseline change minus the median change of peers), not a causal estimate.
Panel A bubble size is the number of official, policy-relevant, verbatim-text evidence items that were two-pass scored and agreed in this package, not a market-influence weight.

No FRED or other API key, and no licensed dataset, is in this package. Firecrawl was not used in Phase 3 (all fetches were curl to official sites). Phase-1/2 Firecrawl use for a few official St. Louis Fed pages remains documented there.

A successful run of the scoring script proves that the arithmetic identities were executed, not that the dimension codes are financially or institutionally 'correct'. Dimension codes are analyst-style judgments from stored official text. The later validation workstream in the Phase-1 build plan has not been run.

events.title: Driving Through Economic Fog (Still)
events.core_quote: At our last meeting, with risks to both the labor market and inflation, and the outlook foggy, it felt prudent to hold rates and await more clarity on how we should be leaning to best support the economy going forward.

events.title: Why Hike?
events.venue: Not fully extracted from the page header in this pass; official Richmond Fed speech page
events.core_quote: The risks to inflation outweigh the risks to maximum employment. That’s why we raised rates.

events.title: The Rooms Driving the Economy
events.venue: Official Richmond Fed speech page 'The Rooms Driving the Economy' (local Fifth District audience; exact hall not separately restated here)
events.core_quote: In sum, today, with demand healthy and inflation stubbornly elevated, the appropriate direction of monetary policy is relatively straightforward. However, risks to the demand outlook remain easy to envision. Because of that, it is wise to move policy with care.
events.final_status: nicht aufgelöst / unresolved — excluded from calculations

events.title: Opening remarks by Governor Barr at a Fed Listens event hosted by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City
events.core_quote: Monetary policy is well positioned to allow us to wait and see how economic conditions unfold.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on the economic outlook
events.core_quote: At our last meeting in September, we decided to reduce the policy rate by 25 basis points, a decision I supported. Monetary policy was and remains modestly restrictive, so it seemed to me appropriate to move the rate a bit closer toward neutral, pending more data and further developments on the economy, the forecast, and the balance of risks.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on artificial intelligence and the labor market
events.core_quote: Based on current conditions and the data in hand, it will likely be appropriate to hold rates steady for some time as we assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on the economic outlook and community development
events.core_quote: I supported this decision, and it is my view that we may need to keep rates steady for some time as we assess economic conditions.

events.title: Brief remarks by Governor Barr on the economic outlook and monetary policy
events.core_quote: As you know, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) met last week and chose to maintain the current setting of monetary policy—a decision I supported. Uncertainty about how these developments will unfold is just one of the reasons why I thought it necessary to hold policy steady at least week's FOMC meeting.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on the economic outlook and financial inclusion
events.core_quote: With inflation above target for a protracted period, there is a risk of broader price pressures taking hold, a risk I am watching closely. However, if inflation appears not to be moderating sufficiently, then I think we should act decisively to raise rates.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on housing
events.core_quote: The FOMC took important action to that end last week by increasing the policy rate, which I supported.

events.title: Speech by Governor Barr on community development investments
events.core_quote: If the economy evolves as I currently forecast, I expect it will be appropriate to raise rates further to achieve that goal on behalf of the American people.

events.title: Speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman on monetary policy and banking
events.core_quote: I supported this decision because the data shows a solid labor market and I would like to see further confirmation that inflation is close to our 2 percent target on a sustained basis.

events.title: FOMC dissent: preferred lower 25bp
events.core_quote: Voting against this action were Michelle W. Bowman and Christopher J. Waller, who preferred to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.

events.title: Speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman on the economic outlook and community banking
events.core_quote: As my dissent statement notes, with economic growth slowing this year and signs of a less dynamic labor market becoming clear, I see it as appropriate to begin gradually moving our moderately restrictive policy stance toward a neutral setting. A proactive approach in moving policy closer to neutral, from its current moderately restrictive stance, would help avoid a further unnecessary erosion in labor market conditions.

events.title: Speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman on the economic outlook
events.core_quote: In my view, the Committee should have begun lowering the policy rate at the July meeting, so, of course, I supported reducing the policy rate at this meeting. In light of all these considerations, in my view, it was appropriate to begin the process of moving policy toward a more neutral stance at this meeting, and it has been for several months.

events.title: Speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman on the outlook for the economy and monetary policy
events.core_quote: At our FOMC meeting this week, my colleagues and I voted to hold the federal funds rate target range at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent. I continue to see policy as moderately restrictive, and, looking ahead to 2026, my Summary of Economic Projections includes three cuts for this year.

events.title: Speech by Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman on monetary policy
events.core_quote: It is appropriate to look through temporarily elevated inflation readings largely due to higher energy prices, provided that we remain credible in our commitment to achieve our inflation goal and one-off tariff effects wane, as I expect. For now, our moderately restrictive policy stance is intended to help maintain stable labor market conditions while allowing inflation to resume its downward trend toward 2 percent once the effects of tariffs and oil prices dissipate.

events.title: The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy
events.venue: C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations, Washington, D.C.; identical remarks later the same day at Unleash Prosperity Now
events.core_quote: Today, I am seeing signs that inflation pressures are persisting, while labor market conditions appear to be firming. This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2 percent.

events.title: Collins prepared remarks 2025-06-24
events.core_quote: The modestly restrictive stance of monetary policy, while necessary, limits in the near term the expansion of housing supply needed to alleviate some of the pressures in the housing market.

events.title: Perspectives on the Economy from Susan M. Collins
events.core_quote: Focusing on the Fed’s congressionally mandated goals of price stability and maximum employment, I see monetary policy as currently well positioned, and I supported last week’s FOMC decision to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 4¼ to 4½ percent. I believe a careful, patient, and highly attentive approach to monetary policy remains appropriate at this point, as we learn more about tariffs and other changes in government policies, and actively assess their implications for the economy. For now, however, I see the current monetary policy stance as modestly restrictive, and well positioned to address a range of possible outcomes.

events.title: Collins prepared remarks 2025-07-15
events.core_quote: Thus, in my view, an “actively patient” approach to monetary policy remains appropriate at this time.

events.title: Views on Current Economic Conditions and Monetary Policy

scores.title: The Economic Outlook and Some Comments on My Policy Communication
scores.a_rationale: Near-term path is stated only as conditionals: inclined to hold if August inflation progress continues, and a hike may be appropriate if that improvement proves fleeting. Under the spec, conditionals are not the baseline, so preferred path and timing are not observed. Upside inflation risks are stated; activity and the labor market 'are not a large factor'. Policy is 'currently only slightly restricting aggregate demand'. He explains that reaction function explicitly.
scores.b_rationale: Although both hold and hike are conditional on August inflation, he also says policy is only slightly restricting demand and that it may not take much inflation acceleration to nudge him into tighter policy, with labor and activity 'not a large factor'. That is treated as a mild tightening bias on the preferred path, not as an unobserved dimension. Timing is still not observed (the September meeting is the decision date, not an urgency claim). Upside inflation risks and the slightly-restrictive assessment are observed, as is the stated reaction function.

scores.a_rationale: The speech is mainly about how to communicate a path. The 'three 25bp hikes / 75bp over six months' figures are introduced with 'let's assume' as an illustration, not as his baseline recommendation, so they are not scored as a preferred path. He does explain a data-dependent way of signaling a likely terminal increment. Forward path, timing, current risk balance and current restrictiveness are not observed as his own baseline.
scores.b_rationale: The 75bp / three-hike figures are presented as an assumed illustration of communication methods ('let's assume'), not as Waller's own baseline path, and are not scored as a path. A data-dependent way of signaling a likely total increment is a reaction-function/communication observation only.

Tightening is needed 'sooner rather than later'. Inflation is 'the focus of my attention'. Further tightening is needed, which is scored as policy not yet tight enough. The 50bp option is a stated branch if October core CPI is around 0.3 percent or higher, and is not the baseline path. 'Sooner rather than later' and the December date are a strong timing signal. Inflation is the focus of attention; further tightening is needed.

vorbehalte: Weights (40/20/20/10/10), camp thresholds (±20), alert thresholds (15 / 25 points) and the 30-day half-life are proposed model parameters and are not validated (nicht validiert / not validated).

Structural lean is the equal-weighted average of agreed event scores in the 12–18 month window 20 May 2025 to 20 November 2026. It is published only when there are at least 4 agreed scored policy events and at least 365 days between the first and last of those events. Shorter official tenure (Warsh as Chair from 22 May 2026; Venable as Interim Atlanta President, first official message 12 May 2026) is labelled insufficient evidence even if a current stance can be computed.

Current stance is the 90-day decay-weighted average of agreed event scores (half-life 30 days). A current-stance camp is printed only when a published stance exists and at least one agreed event in that 90-day window has an observed preferred-rate-path dimension (same rule as Phase 2). That camp is not a structural classification.
The public camp field is the structural classification (Hawk / Centrist / Dove / insufficient evidence). Current stance and its camp are shown alongside it.

Phase-2 events keep their original independent Pass A and Pass B. A reasoned third pass was run on the seven Phase-2 disagreements. Five were resolved by 2-of-3 agreement and are included with recomputed scores. Two (Schmid 15.11.2026 and Barkin 9.11.2026) remain nicht aufgelöst / unresolved and are excluded from calculations.

Phase 3.1 is a delta rerun that two-pass scored remaining policy-relevant official texts already stored under phase3/raw/ for 20 May 2025–20 November 2026. No new crawl was run. Two FOMC statements (17 June and 16 September 2026) were re-fetched with curl only to confirm the official 12-0 votes; no missed dissents were found. Pass A and Pass B were coded from the same official verbatim quotes with a conservative rubric (conditional scenarios are not a baseline path; missing dimensions stay not_observed, never 0). They agree where that official language is explicit. Identical or near-verbatim repeat speeches and official dissent explainers already scored in v3 were treated as syndication and excluded from the calculations. Official texts with no observed dimension, and non-policy official texts, are listed internally and are not in the public events table.

Every scored quote used in site_data_v3_1 is verbatim from an official Board or Reserve Bank page, official PDF, or FOMC statement stored in this package. Licensed-press wording is not in site_data_v3_1. Interviews without an official transcript remain unconfirmed and are not scored. A primary-source date correction was applied to one Kansas City speech: the stored filename used 12 November 2026, but the official datePublished is 18 September 2026.

Speeches without monetary-policy path or stance content stay out of the public events table. Missing dimensions are coded 'not observed', never 0. Allowed dimension codes are {-2,-1,+1,+2} or not_observed.

Event scores use observed dimensions only, with weights renormalised and then scaled by 1/2 to the -100..+100 range. A single observed dimension therefore renormalises to ±50 or ±100. Coverage and confidence are published with the score.

2026 voter status is taken from the official FOMC membership page (federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomc.htm, last update 18 November 2026). The seven Board seats are filled (no vacancy). Cheryl Venable is Interim President of the Atlanta Fed. Sushmita Shukla is listed as a 2026 alternate (New York First Vice President) but is not a president and is not scored. Primary-source dates are used throughout.
Relative shift is a diagnostic (own latest-vs-baseline change minus the median change of peers), not a causal estimate.
Panel A bubble size is the number of official, policy-relevant, verbatim-text evidence items that were two-pass scored and agreed in this package, not a market-influence weight.

No FRED or other API key, and no licensed dataset, is in this package. Firecrawl was not used in Phase 3 (all fetches were curl to official sites). Phase-1/2 Firecrawl use for a few official St. Louis Fed pages remains documented there.

A successful run of the scoring script proves that the arithmetic identities were executed, not that the dimension codes are financially or institutionally 'correct'. Dimension codes are analyst-style judgments from stored official text. The later validation workstream in the Phase-1 build plan has not been run.
